cols.sub: From his ﷺ life, in the order it happened

cols.title: The Prophets عليهم السلام

cols.title: The awliya
cols.sub: The friends of Allah, from the Tabi'in to our own time

stories.title: The cloak and the Black Stone
text: When Quraysh rebuilt the Ka'bah, every clan wanted the honour of setting the Black Stone back in its place. The argument went on for four nights, and swords were close to being drawn.

The oldest man among them, Abu Umayyah ibn al-Mughirah, said: let the first man to walk in through the gate decide between you. They agreed, and the first to enter was Muhammad ﷺ. They were relieved and said, "This is al-Amin, the trustworthy one. We accept him."

He ﷺ spread his cloak on the ground and placed the Stone on it. Then he ﷺ asked the leader of each clan to take hold of an edge, and together they lifted it. When it reached its place, he ﷺ set it there with his own hands. No one was left out, and no blood was shed.
stories.lesson: Long before revelation, his ﷺ honesty had already won people's trust. Wisdom finds a way for everyone to share in what is good.
stories.src: Nur al-Yaqin, Shaykh Muhammad al-Khudari: the rebuilding of the Ka'bah

stories.title: "Allah will never disgrace you"
text: The first revelation came in the cave of Hira'. The Prophet ﷺ returned home trembling and said to Khadijah رضي الله عنها, "Cover me, cover me." When the fear had passed he ﷺ told her what had happened and said, "I feared for myself."

Khadijah رضي الله عنها answered with certainty. She did not point to wealth or family. She pointed to his ﷺ character: "Never! By Allah, Allah will never disgrace you. You keep ties with your relatives, you carry the burdens of the weak, you give to those who have nothing, you honour your guests, and you help people when calamity strikes."
She was the first person to believe in him ﷺ, and he ﷺ never forgot her loyalty for the rest of his life.
stories.lesson: Good character is a protection. Those who serve people are not abandoned by Allah.
stories.src: Sahih al-Bukhari, the beginning of revelation (hadith 3)
stories.ar: كَلَّا وَاللَّهِ مَا يُخْزِيكَ اللَّهُ أَبَدًا

stories.title: The du'a at Ta'if
text: After years of rejection in Makkah, the Prophet ﷺ walked to Ta'if with Zayd ibn Harithah رضي الله عنه, hoping its people would listen. Their leaders answered him harshly, then sent their children and servants to line the road and throw stones at him ﷺ until his feet bled. Zayd رضي الله عنه tried to shield him.

He ﷺ sat in the shade of a vineyard and turned to his Lord. He ﷺ did not complain about the people. He ﷺ said, in part: "If You are not angry with me, I do not mind. But Your well-being is wider for me."

The owners of the vineyard sent their servant 'Addas with a bunch of grapes. The Prophet ﷺ began with "Bismillah", spoke to him of the Prophet Yunus عليه السلام, and 'Addas accepted Islam on the spot.
Later the angel of the mountains came and offered to crush the town between its two mountains. He ﷺ replied, "No. I hope that Allah will bring from their descendants people who worship Allah alone."
stories.lesson: On the hardest day, his ﷺ concern was only for Allah's pleasure, and for the people who had hurt him.
stories.src: Nur al-Yaqin: the journey to Ta'if; and Sahih al-Bukhari (hadith 3231)
stories.ar: إِنْ لَمْ تَكُنْ سَاخِطًا عَلَيَّ فَلَا أُبَالِي، غَيْرَ أَنَّ عَافِيَتَكَ هِيَ أَوْسَعُ لِي
links: seerah|4|The Year of Sorrow and Ta'if

stories.title: Two, and Allah is their third
text: On the night of the Hijrah, the Prophet ﷺ and Abu Bakr رضي الله عنه hid in the cave of Thawr. Quraysh had offered a great reward for them, and search parties combed the mountains.
The searchers came right up to the mouth of the cave. Abu Bakr رضي الله عنه could see their feet and whispered, "O Messenger of Allah ﷺ, if one of them looked down at his feet, he would see us."

The Prophet ﷺ answered calmly: "What do you think, Abu Bakr, of two whose third is Allah?" Allah tells of that moment in the Qur'an: "Do not grieve; Allah is with us." The searchers turned away and never looked down.
stories.lesson: Tawakkul is not the absence of danger. It is a heart at rest because it knows Allah is near.
stories.src: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Tafsir, Surat al-Tawbah (hadith 4663)
stories.ar: مَا ظَنُّكَ بِاثْنَيْنِ اللَّهُ ثَالِثُهُمَا
links: seerah|6|The Night Journey and the Hijrah
sahabah|1|Abu Bakr al-Siddiq رضي الله عنه

stories.title: Suraqah's horse
text: Once the search died down, the Prophet ﷺ and Abu Bakr رضي الله عنه set out for Madinah along the coast. Quraysh had promised a hundred camels for each of them, dead or captured.
Suraqah ibn Malik heard they had been seen and rode after them, hoping for the prize. As he came close, his horse's legs sank into the ground and he fell. He tried again, and again the horse sank.

Suraqah understood that they were protected. He called out, asked for safety, and offered them supplies. The Prophet ﷺ asked only that he keep their route secret. Suraqah went back and turned every other searcher away, and in time he became a Muslim himself.
stories.lesson: Whoever Allah protects cannot be reached. Even the one who comes to harm may leave as a guard.
stories.src: Nur al-Yaqin: the Hijrah of the Prophet ﷺ
links: seerah|6|The Night Journey and the Hijrah

stories.title: The tree trunk that wept
text: In the early days in Madinah, the Prophet ﷺ would lean against the trunk of a date palm in the masjid when he ﷺ gave the khutbah.
Later a minbar was made for him ﷺ. The first time he ﷺ stood on it, the companions heard the old trunk cry out, moaning like a camel longing for its young, until the whole masjid could hear it.

The Prophet ﷺ came down, went to the trunk and held it, and it grew quiet like a child being soothed. Al-Hasan al-Basri رحمه الله would weep when he told this story and say: "O servants of Allah, a piece of wood longs for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. You have more right to long for him."
Qadi 'Iyad رحمه الله notes that this report is mutawatir, narrated by so many that it cannot be doubted.
stories.lesson: Love for the Prophet ﷺ is part of faith. If wood could long for him ﷺ, our hearts should too.
stories.src: al-Shifa, Qadi 'Iyad: the moaning of the palm trunk

stories.title: Water from between his fingers
text: On more than one journey, the companions ran short of water when the time for prayer came. All that could be found was a little water in a small vessel.

The Prophet ﷺ placed his blessed hand in the vessel, and water began to flow from between his fingers like a spring. The companions came one after another and made wudu, and there was enough for all of them.
When Jabir رضي الله عنه was asked how many they had been, he said they had been fifteen hundred, and that it would have been enough even for a hundred thousand.
stories.lesson: Allah honoured His Messenger ﷺ with signs that people saw with their own eyes. Barakah is from Allah, and it came through him ﷺ.
stories.src: al-Shifa, Qadi 'Iyad: water flowing from between his ﷺ fingers

stories.title: Jabir's small meal
text: While the Muslims dug the trench around Madinah, food was so scarce that the Prophet ﷺ had tied a stone to his stomach against hunger. Jabir رضي الله عنه saw this and went home. He and his wife had only a measure of barley and a young goat.

Jabir quietly invited the Prophet ﷺ and one or two others. But the Prophet ﷺ called out to all the diggers: "Jabir has made food. Come!" Jabir's wife was worried, but the Prophet ﷺ told them not to take the pot off the fire or bake the bread until he ﷺ arrived.

He ﷺ blessed the dough and the pot, and the food was served in turns. Jabir later swore by Allah that a thousand men ate until they were full and left, and the pot was still bubbling and the dough still being baked as before.
stories.lesson: Give what you have, however little. Barakah comes with sincerity and generosity.
stories.src: al-Shifa, Qadi 'Iyad: the increase of food

stories.title: "Go, you are free"
text: For twenty years Quraysh had mocked the Prophet ﷺ, tortured his companions, driven him ﷺ from his home and fought against him ﷺ. Now he ﷺ entered Makkah at the head of ten thousand, with his head lowered in humility.

He ﷺ cleansed the Ka'bah of idols, then stood at its door. The people of Makkah gathered, waiting to hear what would be done with them. He ﷺ asked, "What do you think I will do with you?" They said, "Good. A noble brother, and the son of a noble brother."
He ﷺ said, "Go, for you are free."
stories.lesson: Forgive when you have the power to punish. That is the character of the Prophet ﷺ.
stories.src: Nur al-Yaqin: forgiveness when able to punish; and Sirat Ibn Hisham
stories.ar: اذْهَبُوا فَأَنْتُمُ الطُّلَقَاءُ

stories.title: The bedouin in the masjid
text: A bedouin who knew nothing of the masjid's rules came in and began to urinate in a corner of it. The companions jumped up and shouted at him.
The Prophet ﷺ said, "Leave him. Do not interrupt him." When the man had finished, he ﷺ asked for a bucket of water to be poured over the place.
Then he ﷺ explained gently to the man that masjids are for the remembrance of Allah, prayer and the Qur'an. And he ﷺ told his companions: "You were sent to make things easy, not to make them hard."
stories.lesson: Teach with gentleness. Harshness drives people away; kindness opens hearts.
stories.src: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Wudu (hadith 220)

stories.title: More merciful than a mother
text: Some captives were brought to the Prophet ﷺ. Among them was a woman searching frantically for her baby. When she found a child among the captives, she held it to her chest and fed it.
The Prophet ﷺ turned to his companions and asked, "Do you think this woman would throw her child into a fire?" They said, "No, not if she could stop it."
He ﷺ said, "Allah is more merciful to His servants than this woman is to her child."
stories.lesson: Never despair of Allah's mercy. The love you see in a mother is a small sign of a far greater mercy.
stories.src: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Adab (hadith 5999)

stories.title: In the service of his family
text: Someone asked 'A'ishah رضي الله عنها what the Prophet ﷺ did at home. She said: "He ﷺ was in the service of his family."
Other narrations add that he ﷺ mended his own clothes, repaired his sandals, milked his goat and served himself, like any other man in his house.
"And when the time for prayer came," she said, "he ﷺ went out to the prayer."
stories.lesson: Greatness is not shown by being served. The best of creation ﷺ served his family.
stories.src: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of the Adhan (hadith 676)

stories.title: Ten years without a harsh word
text: Anas ibn Malik رضي الله عنه was a young boy when his mother brought him to serve the Prophet ﷺ in Madinah. He served him ﷺ for ten years.
Anas said: "In all that time he ﷺ never once said 'uff' to me. He ﷺ never said about something I had done, 'Why did you do that?', or about something I had left, 'Why did you not do it?'"
He also said the Prophet ﷺ had the best character of all people.
stories.lesson: The people closest to us see our real character. His ﷺ gentleness never ran out.
stories.src: al-Shama'il al-Muhammadiyyah, Imam al-Tirmidhi: the character of the Messenger ﷺ

stories.title: Passing the ruins of Thamud
text: On the way to Tabuk, the army camped at al-Hijr, the old homes of Thamud, the people of the Prophet Salih عليه السلام who were destroyed for killing the she-camel. The companions drew water from its wells and made dough with it.
The Prophet ﷺ told them to pour the water away and feed the dough to the camels. They were to draw only from the well the she-camel used to drink from.

He ﷺ said, "Do not enter the homes of those who were punished unless you are weeping, in case what befell them befalls you." He ﷺ covered his head and hurried his mount until they had passed through the valley.
stories.lesson: Places of Allah's punishment are not for sightseeing. Pass them with humility and fear of Allah.
stories.src: Qisas al-Anbiya', Ibn Kathir: the Prophet ﷺ passing al-Hijr

stories.title: Two mistakes, two answers
text: Allah created Adam عليه السلام with His own hands, breathed into him of the spirit He created, taught him the names of all things, and commanded the angels to prostrate to him in honour. They all prostrated, except Iblis.
Asked why, Iblis said, "I am better than him. You created me from fire and him from clay." He did not admit his wrong. He argued, and he was cast out.

Adam عليه السلام and his wife were told they could eat from anything in the Garden except one tree. Shaytan whispered to them and they ate from it. When they realised, they did not argue or blame. They turned straight back to Allah and said: "Our Lord, we have wronged ourselves. If You do not forgive us and have mercy on us, we will surely be among the losers."
Allah accepted their repentance, for He is the Ever-Relenting, the Most Merciful.
stories.lesson: Everyone slips. Iblis answered his mistake with pride; Adam عليه السلام answered his with repentance. Be a child of Adam.
stories.src: Qisas al-Anbiya', Ibn Kathir: the creation of Adam عليه السلام
stories.ar: رَبَّنَا ظَلَمْنَا أَنفُسَنَا وَإِن لَّمْ تَغْفِرْ لَنَا وَتَرْحَمْنَا لَنَكُونَنَّ مِنَ الْخَاسِرِينَ

stories.person: The sons of Adam عليه السلام
stories.title: The first envy
text: The two sons of Adam عليه السلام each offered a sacrifice to Allah. It was accepted from one and not from the other.

The one whose offering was refused was eaten up by envy and said, "I will kill you." His brother answered, "Allah only accepts from those who fear Him. Even if you raise your hand to kill me, I will not raise mine to kill you. I fear Allah, the Lord of the worlds."

Envy won, and he killed his brother. Then he did not know what to do with the body, until Allah sent a crow scratching at the ground. He cried, "Woe to me! Am I not even able to be like this crow and bury my brother?" And he became one of the regretful.
stories.lesson: Envy starts small in the heart and can end in disaster. Ask Allah to accept your deeds rather than resenting what He gives others.
stories.src: Qisas al-Anbiya', Ibn Kathir: the two sons of Adam

stories.title: Nine hundred and fifty years
text: Nuh عليه السلام called his people to worship Allah alone for nine hundred and fifty years: by night and by day, in public and in private. Most of them put their fingers in their ears and covered themselves with their clothes so they would not hear.
When the command came, he built the ark while his people mocked him. Then the water burst from the earth and poured from the sky, and the ark sailed on waves like mountains.

Nuh عليه السلام saw his own son standing apart and called to him: "My son, come aboard with us, and do not be with the disbelievers." His son said he would climb a mountain to escape the water. The waves came between them, and he was among those who drowned.
stories.lesson: Keep calling to the good, however long it takes. Guidance is in Allah's hands alone, even for a prophet's own child.
stories.src: Qisas al-Anbiya', Ibn Kathir: the story of Nuh عليه السلام
stories.ar: يَا بُنَيَّ ارْكَب مَّعَنَا وَلَا تَكُن مَّعَ الْكَافِرِينَ

stories.title: "Allah is enough for us"
text: As a young man, Ibrahim عليه السلام broke his people's idols, leaving only the largest, to show them that their gods could not even protect themselves.
Furious, they built an enormous fire, so large that it took days to gather the wood. They bound Ibrahim عليه السلام and threw him into it from a catapult.

As he was thrown, he said: "Allah is enough for us, and the best one to rely on." Allah said: "O fire, be coolness and safety for Ibrahim." The fire burned only the ropes that bound him, and he walked out unharmed.
stories.lesson: Those words were said again by the Prophet ﷺ and his companions when they were told an army had gathered against them. They are words for every frightening moment.
stories.src: Qisas al-Anbiya', Ibn Kathir: Ibrahim عليه السلام and the fire, citing Sahih al-Bukhari
stories.ar: حَسْبُنَا اللَّهُ وَنِعْمَ الْوَكِيلُ

stories.title: The king who argued about his Lord
text: A tyrant king, whom the scholars name as Namrud, claimed to be a lord himself. Ibrahim عليه السلام told him, "My Lord is the One who gives life and causes death."
The king said, "I give life and cause death too." He meant he could spare a condemned man or have another killed.
So Ibrahim عليه السلام said: "Allah brings the sun from the east. Then you bring it from the west." The disbeliever was left speechless.
stories.lesson: Truth does not need anger. Clear, calm reasoning leaves falsehood with nothing to say.
stories.src: Qisas al-Anbiya', Ibn Kathir: Ibrahim's debate

stories.title: "Then He will not abandon us"
text: By Allah's command, Ibrahim عليه السلام brought his wife Hajar and their baby Isma'il to an empty valley where Makkah stands today. There was no water and no one living there. He left them with a bag of dates and a skin of water and turned to go.

Hajar followed him, asking again and again, "Will you leave us in this valley with no people and nothing?" He did not answer. Then she asked, "Did Allah command you to do this?" He said yes. She said, "Then He will not abandon us," and went back.

When the water ran out and the baby began to suffer, she ran between the hills of Safa and Marwah, searching, seven times. Then she heard a sound and found an angel at the place of Zamzam, digging with his heel until water gushed out. The Prophet ﷺ said: "That is why people go between them", in the sa'y of Hajj and 'Umrah.
stories.lesson: Tawakkul and effort go together. She trusted Allah completely, and she still ran.
stories.src: Qisas al-Anbiya', Ibn Kathir, citing Sahih al-Bukhari

stories.title: "Do as you are commanded"
text: Ibrahim عليه السلام had waited many years for a son. When Isma'il عليه السلام was old enough to walk and work beside him, Ibrahim saw in a dream that he was sacrificing him, and the dreams of prophets are revelation.
He told his son, "I have seen in a dream that I am sacrificing you. What do you think?" Isma'il answered: "My father, do as you are commanded. You will find me, if Allah wills, among the patient."
When both had submitted and Ibrahim laid him down, Allah called out that he had fulfilled the vision, and ransomed Isma'il with a great sacrifice. Muslims remember it every Eid al-Adha.
stories.lesson: True submission means putting Allah's command above what we love most. And Allah does not let such submission go unrewarded.
stories.src: Qisas al-Anbiya', Ibn Kathir: the sacrifice
stories.ar: يَا أَبَتِ افْعَلْ مَا تُؤْمَرُ سَتَجِدُنِي إِن شَاءَ اللَّهُ مِنَ الصَّابِرِينَ

stories.title: Building the House
text: Years later, Ibrahim عليه السلام returned to Makkah and told Isma'il that Allah had commanded them to build a House there. Isma'il carried the stones and Ibrahim laid them.
When the walls grew high, Ibrahim stood on a stone to keep building. That stone is the Maqam Ibrahim, still beside the Ka'bah.
As they worked, circling the House, the two of them kept repeating: "Our Lord, accept this from us. You are the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing."
stories.lesson: Two prophets built the House of Allah, and still they asked Him to accept it. Do good, then worry about whether it is accepted, not about being praised.
stories.src: Qisas al-Anbiya', Ibn Kathir, citing Sahih al-Bukhari
stories.ar: رَبَّنَا تَقَبَّلْ مِنَّا إِنَّكَ أَنتَ السَّمِيعُ الْعَلِيمُ

stories.title: "I seek refuge in Allah"
text: Yusuf عليه السلام grew up in the house of the 'Aziz of Egypt, who had bought him as a boy. When he became a young man, the wife of the 'Aziz tried to seduce him. She closed the doors and called him to herself.
Yusuf عليه السلام said: "I seek refuge in Allah! He is my lord, who gave me a good home. Wrongdoers never succeed." He ran for the door.
She threatened him with prison if he did not obey her. Yusuf عليه السلام said: "My Lord, prison is dearer to me than what they invite me to." He chose years in a cell over one moment of disobedience.
stories.lesson: The Prophet ﷺ said that one of the seven Allah will shade on the Day of Judgement is a man invited to sin who says, "I fear Allah."
stories.src: Qisas al-Anbiya', Ibn Kathir: the story of Yusuf عليه السلام
stories.ar: رَبِّ السِّجْنُ أَحَبُّ إِلَيَّ مِمَّا يَدْعُونَنِي إِلَيْهِ

stories.title: "No blame on you today"
text: Yusuf's brothers had thrown him into a well as a boy out of jealousy. Years later, during a famine, they came to Egypt to beg for grain, not knowing that the minister in charge of the storehouses was Yusuf عليه السلام himself.
When at last he told them who he was, they were overcome with shame and said, "By Allah, Allah has preferred you over us, and we were truly in the wrong."

Yusuf عليه السلام did not list their crimes or make them pay. He said: "No blame on you today. May Allah forgive you; He is the Most Merciful of the merciful." On the day he conquered Makkah, the Prophet ﷺ quoted these same words to Quraysh.
stories.lesson: Forgiveness is strongest when you have the power to take revenge.
stories.src: Qisas al-Anbiya', Ibn Kathir: the story of Yusuf عليه السلام
stories.ar: لَا تَثْرِيبَ عَلَيْكُمُ الْيَوْمَ يَغْفِرُ اللَّهُ لَكُمْ وَهُوَ أَرْحَمُ الرَّاحِمِينَ

stories.title: The patience of Ayyub
text: Allah gave Ayyub عليه السلام wealth, land and many children. Then, as a test, it was all taken from him. He also suffered a long illness, until only his faithful wife stayed by his side.

Through all those years he did not complain about Allah to anyone. When he finally called on his Lord, he did so with the gentlest words: "Harm has touched me, and You are the Most Merciful of the merciful."

Allah answered him: "Strike the ground with your foot." A spring came up to wash in and drink from, and he was healed. Allah returned his family to him and the like of them with them, as a mercy. And Allah said of him: "We found him patient. What an excellent servant!"
stories.lesson: Patience is not silence about pain. It is bringing the pain to Allah alone.
stories.src: Qisas al-Anbiya', Ibn Kathir: the story of Ayyub عليه السلام
stories.ar: أَنِّي مَسَّنِيَ الضُّرُّ وَأَنتَ أَرْحَمُ الرَّاحِمِينَ

stories.title: In three darknesses
text: Yunus عليه السلام called his people for a long time, and they refused. He left them in anger, before Allah had given him permission, and boarded a laden ship.
A storm rose. The passengers drew lots to lighten the ship, and the lot fell on Yunus عليه السلام. He was thrown into the sea and swallowed by a great fish.

In the darkness of the night, the sea and the belly of the fish, he called out: "There is no god but You. Glory be to You. I have been among the wrongdoers." Allah answered him and saved him. The Prophet ﷺ said that no Muslim calls with this du'a for anything without Allah answering him.
stories.lesson: However deep the darkness, it is never too dark to call on Allah, or too late to admit a mistake.
stories.src: Qisas al-Anbiya', Ibn Kathir: the story of Yunus عليه السلام
stories.ar: لَّا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا أَنتَ سُبْحَانَكَ إِنِّي كُنتُ مِنَ الظَّالِمِينَ

stories.title: A basket on the river
text: Pharaoh had ordered that the baby boys of the Children of Israel be killed. When Musa عليه السلام was born, Allah inspired his mother: "Nurse him, and when you fear for him, put him in the river. Do not fear and do not grieve. We will return him to you and make him one of the messengers."
She placed him in a basket and set it on the Nile. It floated to the very palace of Pharaoh, where his wife Asiyah took him in and loved him.

The baby refused every nurse they brought. Musa's sister, who had followed the basket, said, "Shall I show you a family who will look after him?" So Musa عليه السلام was returned to his own mother's arms, and she was even paid to nurse him.
stories.lesson: When Allah's promise seems impossible, trust it. He can bring your hope back to you through your enemy's own house.
stories.src: Qisas al-Anbiya', Ibn Kathir: the story of Musa عليه السلام

stories.title: "I am in need of whatever good You send"
text: Musa عليه السلام fled Egypt alone, hungry and with nothing. At the wells of Madyan he found shepherds crowding the water, while two young women held back their flock and waited.
He asked them why, and they said they could not water their sheep until the shepherds had gone, and their father was a very old man. Musa عليه السلام watered their flock for them.

Then he went back to the shade and said: "My Lord, I am in need of whatever good You send down to me." Soon afterwards one of the women came, walking shyly, to say that her father wanted to reward him. It led to shelter, work and marriage.
stories.lesson: Help others even when you are in need yourself, then ask Allah alone. Musa عليه السلام asked no one but Him.
stories.src: Qisas al-Anbiya', Ibn Kathir: Musa عليه السلام in Madyan
stories.ar: رَبِّ إِنِّي لِمَا أَنزَلْتَ إِلَيَّ مِنْ خَيْرٍ فَقِيرٌ

stories.title: "My Lord is with me"
text: Musa عليه السلام led the Children of Israel out of Egypt by night. At sunrise they reached the sea, and behind them they saw Pharaoh's army coming.
His people panicked: "We will be overtaken!" The sea was in front of them and the army behind them.

Musa عليه السلام said: "Never! My Lord is with me. He will guide me." Allah told him to strike the sea with his staff. It split into paths, each side standing like a great mountain, and they crossed on dry ground. When Pharaoh followed, the sea closed over him and his army.
stories.lesson: When every way out seems closed, the believer still says: my Lord is with me.
stories.src: Qisas al-Anbiya', Ibn Kathir: the drowning of Pharaoh
stories.ar: كَلَّا إِنَّ مَعِيَ رَبِّي سَيَهْدِينِ

stories.title: The teacher by the sea
text: Musa عليه السلام was once asked who the most knowledgeable person was, and said, "I am." Allah told him there was a servant of His, at the meeting of the two seas, who had knowledge Musa did not. So Musa set out to learn from him: al-Khidr.

Al-Khidr agreed on one condition: "Do not ask me about anything until I explain it to you." Then he made a hole in the boat of the poor men who had carried them for free. He killed a boy. And in a town that refused them food, he rebuilt a falling wall for nothing. Each time, Musa عليه السلام could not stay silent.

At last al-Khidr explained. A king was seizing every good boat, and a damaged one would be left to the poor men. The boy would have grown up to bring misery to his believing parents. The wall hid treasure belonging to two orphans, whose father had been righteous.
stories.lesson: Even a great prophet travelled to learn. What looks like harm may be mercy we cannot yet see.
stories.src: Qisas al-Anbiya', Ibn Kathir: Musa and al-Khidr, citing Sahih al-Bukhari

stories.title: A king who earned with his hands
text: Allah gave Dawud عليه السلام a kingdom, wisdom, and a voice so beautiful that the mountains and birds glorified Allah with him.
Yet he did not live from the treasury. Allah softened iron for him, and he made coats of mail with his own hands and lived from what he earned.
The Prophet ﷺ said: "No one has ever eaten better food than what he eats from the work of his own hands. And the Prophet of Allah Dawud used to eat from the work of his own hands."
stories.lesson: Honest work is honourable, whoever you are. Halal earning is part of worship.
stories.src: Qisas al-Anbiya', Ibn Kathir, citing Sahih al-Bukhari

stories.title: The ant
text: Sulayman عليه السلام was given a kingdom no one after him would have. Jinn, people and birds marched in his army, and he understood the speech of birds and animals.
Once his army came to a valley of ants. An ant called out, "Ants, go into your homes, so that Sulayman and his army do not crush you without realising."

Sulayman عليه السلام smiled at her words. He did not boast of his power. He turned to his Lord and said: "My Lord, inspire me to be grateful for Your favour which You have given me and my parents, and to do good that pleases You."
stories.lesson: The more Allah gives you, the more grateful and gentle you should become, even towards an ant.
stories.src: Qisas al-Anbiya', Ibn Kathir: the story of Sulayman عليه السلام
stories.ar: رَبِّ أَوْزِعْنِي أَنْ أَشْكُرَ نِعْمَتَكَ الَّتِي أَنْعَمْتَ عَلَيَّ

stories.title: "I am the servant of Allah"
text: Maryam عليها السلام gave birth to 'Isa alone, under a date palm, in great pain. She was told: "Shake the trunk of the palm towards you, and fresh ripe dates will fall for you. Eat, drink, and be at peace."
When she brought the baby to her people, they accused her. She did not answer them; she pointed to the child. They said, "How can we speak to a baby in the cradle?"
Then the baby 'Isa عليه السلام spoke: "I am the servant of Allah. He has given me the Book and made me a prophet." The very first thing he said about himself was that he was Allah's servant.
stories.lesson: Allah defends the innocent. And 'Isa عليه السلام is a servant and messenger of Allah, as he said himself.
stories.src: Qisas al-Anbiya', Ibn Kathir: the birth of 'Isa عليه السلام
stories.ar: إِنِّي عَبْدُ اللَّهِ آتَانِيَ الْكِتَابَ وَجَعَلَنِي نَبِيًّا

stories.title: The man known in heaven
text: The Prophet ﷺ told 'Umar رضي الله عنه about a man from Yemen named Uwais, of the tribe of Murad and then of Qaran. He had suffered from leprosy and been cured except for a patch the size of a coin. "He has a mother, and he is devoted to her. If he swore by Allah, Allah would fulfil his oath. If you can get him to ask forgiveness for you, do so."

Uwais never met the Prophet ﷺ; he stayed behind to care for his mother. Years later, whenever reinforcements came from Yemen, 'Umar رضي الله عنه asked, "Is Uwais ibn 'Amir among you?" At last he found him, checked every detail, and asked him to pray for his forgiveness. Uwais did.
'Umar offered to write to the governor of Kufah to look after him. Uwais declined: "I prefer to be among ordinary people."
stories.lesson: Unknown on earth, known in heaven. Service to his mother raised him to a station the caliph himself sought.
stories.src: Sahih Muslim, the virtues of Uwais al-Qarani (hadith 2542)

stories.title: The prince who went hunting
text: Ibrahim ibn Adham was a prince of Balkh. One day he rode out to hunt and was chasing a fox or a hare when a voice called out to him: "Ibrahim, is this what you were created for? Is this what you were commanded to do?"
It called again, this time from the pommel of his own saddle: "By Allah, you were not created for this, and this is not what you were commanded."

He got off his horse, met one of his father's shepherds, and swapped his royal clothes for the shepherd's woollen cloak, giving him the horse and everything he had. He went into the desert and on to Makkah, kept company with Sufyan al-Thawri and al-Fudayl ibn 'Iyad, and spent the rest of his life eating only from the work of his hands: harvesting, and guarding orchards.
stories.lesson: Ask yourself what you were created for. Ibrahim answered the question with his whole life.
stories.src: al-Risalah al-Qushayriyyah: the shaykhs of the path, Ibrahim ibn Adham

stories.title: The highwayman and the verse
text: Before he repented, al-Fudayl ibn 'Iyad was a highwayman who robbed travellers between Abiward and Sarakhs.

One night he was climbing a wall to reach a woman he was infatuated with when he heard someone reciting: "Has the time not come for the believers that their hearts should humble themselves to the remembrance of Allah?"

He said, "Yes, my Lord, the time has come," and climbed down. He spent the night in a ruin, where a caravan was camping. He heard them arguing about whether to travel on in the dark: "Fudayl is on the road. He will rob us." Fudayl repented on the spot, told them they were safe from him, and spent the rest of his life beside the Haram in Makkah, where he became one of the great imams of the Ummah.
stories.lesson: No one is too far gone. One verse, heard with an open heart, can change a whole life.
stories.src: al-Risalah al-Qushayriyyah: the shaykhs of the path, al-Fudayl ibn 'Iyad
stories.ar: أَلَمْ يَأْنِ لِلَّذِينَ آمَنُوا أَن تَخْشَعَ قُلُوبُهُمْ لِذِكْرِ اللَّهِ

stories.title: "He is One"
text: Ma'ruf al-Karkhi was born to Christian parents, who sent him as a boy to a teacher. The teacher told him to repeat the words of the Trinity, "the third of three". Ma'ruf kept answering, "No, He is One."
One day the teacher beat him badly, and Ma'ruf ran away. His parents grieved and said, "If only he would come back to us, whatever religion he follows, we would follow it with him."

Ma'ruf accepted Islam at the hands of 'Ali ibn Musa al-Rida, then came home and knocked on the door. "Who is it?" "Ma'ruf." "What religion have you come with?" "The pure religion." And his parents became Muslim. He became one of the great shaykhs of Baghdad, known for his answered du'as, and the teacher of al-Sari al-Saqati.
stories.lesson: Hold to the truth of Tawhid, even as a child and even under pressure. It can bring a whole family to Islam.
stories.src: al-Risalah al-Qushayriyyah: the shaykhs of the path, Ma'ruf al-Karkhi

stories.title: The scrap of paper
text: Bishr ibn al-Harith was walking along a road when he saw a scrap of paper in the dust, trodden underfoot. Written on it was the name of Allah.
He picked it up. He had only one dirham, and he spent it on perfume. He perfumed the paper and placed it high in a crack in a wall, where no one would step on it.

That night he saw in a dream someone saying to him: "Bishr, you perfumed My name. I will make your name fragrant in this world and the next." That was the beginning of his repentance, and his name has been loved by the Muslims ever since.
stories.lesson: Honour what Allah has honoured. A small act of respect, done sincerely, can open a great door.
stories.src: al-Risalah al-Qushayriyyah: the shaykhs of the path, Bishr al-Hafi

stories.title: Thirty years for one alhamdulillah
text: Al-Sari al-Saqati, a shopkeeper in Baghdad and the uncle and teacher of al-Junayd, once said: "For thirty years I have been asking Allah's forgiveness for saying alhamdulillah once."
He was asked how that could be. He said: "A fire broke out in Baghdad. A man met me and said, 'Your shop has been saved.' I said, 'Alhamdulillah.'
"I have regretted it ever since, because I wanted something good for myself over what had befallen the Muslims."
stories.lesson: Real faith means caring for others as for yourself. Even our praise of Allah should not forget other people's pain.
stories.src: al-Risalah al-Qushayriyyah: the shaykhs of the path, al-Sari al-Saqati

stories.title: The servant who was not worried
text: Shaqiq al-Balkhi was the son of a wealthy family of Khurasan. During a famine, when everyone was anxious, he saw a slave playing and cheerful.
"Why are you so happy?" Shaqiq asked. "Can't you see the drought and hunger people are in?" The slave said, "What is that to me? My master owns a whole village, and it brings him everything we need."

Shaqiq thought: if this man's master owns one village, and his master is a poor creature himself, and still he does not worry about his provision, how can a Muslim worry about his, when his Master is the Rich, who owns everything? He took up the path of zuhd and became known for his teaching on tawakkul.
stories.lesson: Worry does not add a crumb to your provision. Work, then trust the One who owns everything.
stories.src: al-Risalah al-Qushayriyyah: the shaykhs of the path, Shaqiq al-Balkhi

stories.title: Three words from an uncle
text: When Sahl ibn 'Abdullah al-Tustari was a small boy, his uncle asked him, "Don't you remember Allah who created you?" "How should I remember Him?" Sahl asked.

His uncle said: "When you turn over in your bed at night, say three times in your heart, without moving your tongue: Allah is with me. Allah is watching me. Allah is my witness." Sahl did so for a few nights. Then his uncle told him to say it seven times, then eleven, and Sahl began to feel a sweetness in his heart.

After a year his uncle said: "Keep what I taught you until you enter the grave." Years later he asked him: "Sahl, would someone who knows Allah is with him, watching and witnessing, disobey Him? Beware of sin." Sahl became one of the great imams of the path.
stories.lesson: Teach children to remember Allah with simple words. Knowing Allah sees you is the root of taqwa.
stories.src: al-Risalah al-Qushayriyyah: the shaykhs of the path, Sahl ibn 'Abdullah al-Tustari
stories.ar: اللَّهُ مَعِي، اللَّهُ نَاظِرٌ إِلَيَّ، اللَّهُ شَاهِدِي

stories.title: "This knowledge of ours is bound by the Book and the Sunnah"
text: Al-Junayd of Baghdad is called the master of the folk of tasawwuf. He learnt the path from his uncle al-Sari al-Saqati and studied fiqh until he could give fatwa.

He laid down a rule that every true shaykh after him has repeated: "Whoever has not memorised the Qur'an and written down the hadith is not to be followed in this matter, because this knowledge of ours is bound by the Book and the Sunnah."
For al-Junayd, tasawwuf was never a way around the Shari'ah. It is the heart of living the Shari'ah sincerely.
stories.lesson: Real tasawwuf stays inside the Qur'an and Sunnah. Anything that leaves them is not the path of the awliya.
stories.src: al-Risalah al-Qushayriyyah: the shaykhs of the path, al-Junayd
links: aqeedah|24|Following the Sunnah and the Jama'ah

stories.title: The professor who left Baghdad
text: Imam al-Ghazali was the most famous scholar of his age, teaching at the great Nizamiyyah college in Baghdad, with hundreds of students and the respect of rulers.

Then he looked honestly at his own heart. He saw that much of his teaching was driven by love of status and fame, not purely for Allah. For months he struggled until his tongue locked and he could no longer lecture or eat properly. At last he gave away his wealth, keeping only what he needed, and left Baghdad in secret.

For about ten years he lived in seclusion in Damascus, Jerusalem and Makkah, purifying his heart. Then he returned to teaching, now for Allah, and wrote the Ihya' 'Ulum al-Din, which has guided the Ummah ever since.
stories.lesson: Sincerity is worth any sacrifice. The greatest scholar of his time began again to make his work purely for Allah.
stories.src: al-Munqidh min al-Dalal, Imam al-Ghazali: the ways of the Sufis

stories.title: Forty dinars sewn in a coat
text: When 'Abd al-Qadir was a young man of about eighteen, he set out from Jilan to study in Baghdad. His mother sewed forty dinars, his share of the inheritance, into the lining of his coat, and made him promise always to tell the truth.

On the way, robbers attacked the caravan. One asked him, "What do you have?" He said, "Forty dinars, sewn under my arm." The robber thought he was joking. Another asked, and he gave the same answer. They took him to their leader, who cut open the lining and found the forty dinars.

"Why did you tell us?" the leader asked. He said, "My mother made me promise to tell the truth, and I will not betray her trust." The leader wept: "You will not betray your promise to your mother, and I have been betraying my promise to my Lord all these years." He repented at the young man's hands, and so did all his men.
stories.lesson: Truthfulness is the first step of the path. One honest young man brought a whole band of robbers to repentance.
stories.src: Bahjat al-Asrar by al-Shattanawfi, and Qala'id al-Jawahir by al-Tadifi: the early life of Shaykh 'Abd al-Qadir

stories.title: The gatherings in Baghdad
text: After many years of study and struggle in Baghdad, Shaykh 'Abd al-Qadir became a great Hanbali faqih and began to teach and preach. His gatherings grew until tens of thousands attended: scholars, rulers, traders and ordinary people.
His biographers report that many Jews and Christians accepted Islam at his hands, and that great numbers of thieves, drinkers and sinners repented in his gatherings.

His message never changed: follow the Qur'an and the Sunnah, guard the obligations, and empty the heart of everything except Allah. His book al-Ghunyah, which is in this app's Library, begins with the fiqh of purification and prayer before it speaks of the heart.
stories.lesson: A true wali calls people back to the Shari'ah and to Allah, never to himself.
stories.src: Bahjat al-Asrar by al-Shattanawfi, and Qala'id al-Jawahir by al-Tadifi

stories.title: The hand from the noble grave
text: Shaykh Ahmad al-Rifa'i, the great wali of Iraq and founder of the Rifa'i path, went on Hajj in the year 555 AH and then visited the Prophet ﷺ in Madinah.

Standing before the noble grave, he recited two lines of poetry. In them he said that while he was far away he used to send his soul to kiss the ground on his behalf; now that he had come in person, he asked the Prophet ﷺ to extend his right hand so that his lips might have their share.

The scholars who recorded it report that the blessed hand came out of the grave, and Shaykh Ahmad kissed it, in front of a great crowd of visitors. Imam al-Suyuti رحمه الله wrote a treatise about this and the other honours Allah gave al-Rifa'i.
stories.lesson: Love of the Prophet ﷺ, with good manners in his ﷺ presence, is the heart of the path of the awliya.
stories.src: al-Sharaf al-Muhattam, Imam al-Suyuti
stories.ar:
فِي حَالَةِ الْبُعْدِ رُوحِي كُنْتُ أُرْسِلُهَا ... تُقَبِّلُ الْأَرْضَ عَنِّي وَهِيَ نَائِبَتِي
وَهَذِهِ دَوْلَةُ الْأَشْبَاحِ قَدْ حَضَرَتْ ... فَامْدُدْ يَمِينَكَ كَيْ تَحْظَى بِهَا شَفَتِي

stories.title: Mercy to a sick dog
text: Shaykh Ahmad al-Rifa'i taught that the shortest way to Allah is humility and brokenness of heart, and his mercy reached every creature.

His biographers tell how he once found a dog covered in mange, which everyone else drove away. He took it outside the town, made it a shelter, washed it with warm water and treated its sores. He fed it and cared for it until it was healed.
When people wondered at a great shaykh nursing a dog, he reminded them that Allah forgave a sinful person for giving water to a thirsty dog, as the Prophet ﷺ told.
stories.lesson: Mercy to creation is a way to the mercy of the Creator.
stories.src: the biographies of Shaykh Ahmad al-Rifa'i
stories.review: Source to confirm: which biography records the dog story

stories.title: From Cyprus to Damascus, and to the world
text: Shaykh Muhammad Nazim 'Adil al-Haqqani was born in Larnaca, Cyprus, in 1922, from a family of scholars. As a young man he studied chemical engineering at the University of Istanbul, while also studying the religious sciences and the path with the scholars of the city.

He felt drawn to Damascus, and there he met Shaykh 'Abdullah al-Fa'iz al-Daghestani of the Naqshbandi path, who became his shaykh. He served him for many years and was sent back to Cyprus to call people to Allah.

For the rest of his long life he travelled, teaching love of Allah and His Messenger ﷺ, respect for the scholars and good manners. From the 1970s he spent many Ramadans in London, and countless people in Britain and around the world came to Islam or returned to their deen through him. He passed away in Lefke, Cyprus, in 2014.
stories.lesson: One sincere servant of Allah, carrying an old path into a new age, can reach the whole world.
stories.src: biographies of Shaykh Nazim written by his students
